pr_title: Bug 4731 Fix Option Expiration Order Tags and Order Event IsAssignment Flag
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->
Standardizes order tags and order events related to option exercise/assignment. All orders/events related to option expiry are now prefix with `Option Expired` and individual events include the following:

OTM: OTM
ITM & long: Automatic Exercise
ITM & short: Automatic Assignment

Since the transaction handler combines the order tag and the order event message, we end up with the following:

Option Expired - OTM
Option Expired - Automatic Exercise
Option Expired - Automatic Assignment

The `OrderEvent.IsAssignment` flag was also updated to only be true in ITM assignment cases.

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
* Add OrderRight.GetExerciseDirection(isShort) extension

> Returns the OrderDirection resulting from exercise/assignment of a particular
option right

* Fix option exercise/assignment order tags and order event messages

> The algorithm manager was doing work to determine whether or not the option ended
in exercise or assignment at expiration. This decision should be left for the exercise
model to decide -- from the algorithm manager's perspective, all that matters is that
the option was expired. The DefaultExerciseModel was updated to properly track whether
the option expired with automatic assignment or exercise, dependending on whether or
not we wrote or bought the option (held liability or right, respectively). Updated unit
tests to check for order event counts and order event messages for option exercise cases.

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
Fixes inaccurate order tags and order event is assignment property

#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->

#### How Has This Been Tested?

<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
Existing unit tests in `SecurityPortfolioManagerTests` expanded to test for the new `OrderEvent.Message` values as well as the `IsAssignment` flag value.

<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
1. When a long OTM option expires, its tag should read option expiration.

2. When a short OTM option expires, its orderevent.IsAssignment should be False.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
1, When a long OTM option expires, the corresponding tag reds `Automatic option exercise on expiration - Adjusting(or removing) the exercised/assigned option`. 

2. When a short OTM option expires, its orderevent.IsAssignment is set to True although no assignment orders take place.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
1. Changing the tag for the options expiration orderevent.

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->

> // TODO : Why doesn't this method take into account the directionality of the quantity like other quantity properties/methods

You are referring to the required `right == OptionRight.Call ? fillQuantity : -fillQuantity`? All consumers of `GetExerciseQuantity` seem to be doing the same operation except for `OptionExerciseOrder` that seems like a bug? 🤔 Agree it kinda feels it should be internal to the `GetExerciseQuantity`

my thoughts exactly -- throughout lean we use `Quantity` to mean the directional quantity and `AbsoluteQuantity` to mean the magnitude of the quantity. I'll put an additional commit in here refactoring this method to follow this convention.
